raw: 45.1 ICS Architecture: SCADA, DCS, PLC, HMI — Definitions and Roles[^208][^209]
teaching_note: ICS describes systems that monitor or control industrial processes; a PLC performs local control, an HMI presents state to a human, and a historian stores observations rather than independently verifying physical truth [@ageint208]. A safety instrumented system provides a protective function distinct from ordinary process control; an architectural claim of independence requires evidence about shared dependencies, not just a separate box. In a wholly fictional, non-executable tank diagram, sensor S reports 40 units to controller C, HMI H displays 40, and historian R records 40: these are three representations of one measurement, not three independent confirmations. A second paper observation of 65 creates an unresolved discrepancy; the asset/consequence row is 'S→C→H/R; visibility disputed; control state unknown; physical harm unestablished', and the analyst records possible sensor, timing, or transcription error, withholds a physical-state conclusion, and sends the question to the designated process-safety reviewer without connecting to or controlling anything. Apply the claim-record procedure in Section [@sec:analytic-workflow] to this evidence boundary.
title: ICS Architecture: SCADA, DCS, PLC, HMI — Definitions and Roles

raw: 45.1.1 SCADA: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition — Large Geographic Systems[^209]
teaching_note: SCADA combines supervisory oversight and data acquisition, often across geographically dispersed assets; it is not synonymous with every industrial controller [@ageint209]. A supervisory display can be stale while local control continues, so loss of visibility and loss of control require separate evidence. Ask which timestamp belongs to the measurement, transport, and display before inferring a process interruption.
title: SCADA: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition — Large Geographic Systems

raw: 45.1.2 DCS: Distributed Control Systems — Chemical, Refining, Power[^209]
teaching_note: A DCS distributes control functions among coordinated components, commonly within a plant; distribution is an architectural property, not a guarantee of independent failure domains [@ageint209]. Several controllers can share power, engineering tools, or configuration dependencies. A paper architecture comparison therefore marks common dependencies rather than counting controllers as redundant protection.
title: DCS: Distributed Control Systems — Chemical, Refining, Power

raw: 45.1.3 PLC: Programmable Logic Controllers — Field-Level Execution[^209]
teaching_note: A PLC processes inputs and executes configured control logic to produce outputs; a log of a requested change does not establish that an output changed or that the physical process followed it [@ageint209]. Distinguish requested, acknowledged, executed, and independently observed states. Classroom records remain inert text: no controller code, device commands, or executable process model is required.
title: PLC: Programmable Logic Controllers — Field-Level Execution

raw: 45.1.4 OT vs. IT: Fundamental Security Philosophy Differences[^209][^210]
teaching_note: OT supports interaction with physical processes, whereas IT emphasizes information processing; the categories overlap, and neither has one universal security-priority ordering [@ageint210]. Safety, availability, integrity, confidentiality, latency, and recovery constraints depend on the process and its hazards. A familiar IT action such as interruption or rapid software change is not automatically safe for OT; analysts identify the constraint and defer any operational decision to authorized engineering and safety personnel.
title: OT and IT: Process-dependent Safety, Availability, and Information Constraints

raw: 45.1.5 Air-Gap Erosion: The Digital Transformation Vulnerability[^209]
teaching_note: An air-gap claim concerns specified connectivity at a specified time; it does not establish the absence of removable-media, maintenance, supply-chain, or human transfer paths. Conversely, a digital-transformation label does not prove that any particular connection exists. In an offline architecture exercise, annotate documented paths and unknown paths separately; do not discover them by scanning or live connection.
title: Air-gap Claims and Changing Connectivity Assumptions

raw: 45.2 Securing ICS: Components, Protocols, Performance, Vulnerability Review[^208]
teaching_note: The cited review discusses components, protocols, design constraints, and defensive approaches; it is not a site-specific safety assessment or proof that a proposed machine-learning control works [@ageint208]. A vulnerability listing identifies a possible software condition, while a process consequence additionally requires exposure, configuration, dependencies, and physical context. Record those missing links instead of multiplying a generic severity score into a physical-loss prediction.
title: Securing ICS: Components, Protocols, Performance, Vulnerability Review

teaching_note: Treat a vendor guide as an attributed account of recommended capabilities, not an independent comparative evaluation [@ageint211]. Asset inventory, segmentation, and monitoring describe different control functions: knowing an asset exists neither blocks access nor proves detection. A defensible comparison identifies what each capability would observe or constrain and leaves effectiveness unknown without applicable evaluation evidence.
title: 2026 Cybersecurity Guide to ICS (Claroty)

raw: 45.4 OT vs. ICS vs. SCADA Security (Palo Alto Networks)[^210]
teaching_note: The cited vendor taxonomy places SCADA within ICS and ICS within the broader OT category [@ageint210]. This is a useful organizing model, not a rule that every real installation has cleanly separated layers. Classify a fictional component by function and dependencies rather than by its product name or vendor category.
title: OT vs. ICS vs. SCADA Security (Palo Alto Networks)

teaching_note: An institutional research page can locate OT expertise and research topics; its existence is not evidence that a specific architecture or response is certified safe [@ageint212]. For the tank example, neither an institutional affiliation nor agreement between copied displays resolves the discrepant measurement. The classroom outcome remains an evidence hold until the designated human reviewer receives an independent, authorized account of process context.
title: Operational Technology Cybersecurity (Idaho National Laboratory)
